_comment: Per-tenant table shardability over the LIVE migration corpus (ADR-0062 "sharded state"; decision-principles.json DP-09). Until governance/check/shardability/tests/shardability_live.rs landed, this doctrine had never produced a verdict about this codebase: the kernel's only Cargo consumer was marketplace/facade/dev-cli, which no workflow invokes, so every case it had ever run was a hand-written fixture in src/lib.rs. Those fixtures are untouched; the live target was ADDED beside them. `frozen_unsharded_tables` maps `<file>::<table>` to the number of CREATE TABLE statements in that file declaring that relation with no `tenant_id` and no `-- shardability: global` opt-out, pinned by EQUALITY over the UNION of the frozen and observed key sets, and therefore TWO-SIDED: a new unsharded table blocks, and a repaired one ALSO blocks until its pin is lowered in the same change. Keys are table-anchored, never line-anchored, so an edit above a CREATE TABLE does not force a blind re-freeze. The min_* floors count SUBJECT MATERIAL (tracked paths, migration files, DDL statements), never findings, so none of them can red on honest progress; there is deliberately NO floor on the violation count and none on the opt-out count, because both have zero as a legitimate target and a floor on a zero-target term reds exactly when the work succeeds.
subject: every tracked *.sql file; every CREATE TABLE statement inside it
_measured_2026_08_19: Measured on dev @ 889027711, the commit that deleted 51 unreferenced product crates and moved every corpus in this repository: 20 tracked *.sql migrations over 13746 tracked paths, 34 CREATE TABLE statements, 0 carrying the `-- shardability: global` opt-out, exactly 1 unsharded. The corpus is small enough that a reviewer can open every subject file by hand, which is the point: this is a finding set that can be checked rather than trusted.
_the_single_finding_and_its_repair: The one finding is `classifier_model_versions` in oya/intelligence/iac/postgres/migrations/guardrails-001-init-schema.sql:117 — a registry of content-safety classifier model versions keyed PRIMARY KEY (model_id, version), with a `pack` column and no tenant dimension anywhere in it. It is genuinely cross-tenant: the same model version is served to every tenant in a pack, so the CORRECT repair is the one-line `-- shardability: global (<reason>)` opt-out marker above the statement, NOT a tenant_id column, which would be a fabricated dimension. That repair is DELIBERATELY NOT MADE HERE. This change connects the doctrine; editing the schema is a separate reviewable decision belonging to whoever owns oya/intelligence's guardrails migrations, and doing it in the same commit would have hidden the connection behind a schema edit. Making it later is a one-line diff plus deleting the one key below.
